The PanoRef coverage optimizer implementation is now a real algorithm (not just occlusion foundation), adding 17 coverage-engine files, a worker, UI, and tests. Joint mode genuinely evaluates candidate pairs rather than greedily selecting the best first origin. Algorithm architecture for normal graybox sets: 8/10; correctness of two search modes: 7.5/10; readiness for complex imported sets: 4/10. Overall: promising but not production-ready yet.

What it got right:
- Surface sampler is deterministic, sampling triangles in proportion to world-space area using barycentric coordinates.
- Origin evaluation includes actual segment occlusion, geometric face normals, viewing angle, approximate projected texel density, separate visibility and usable-coverage bitsets, and continuous quality values.
- Joint-pair mode is genuinely joint: checks every legal coarse pair, ranks by bitset union, then applies quality and contribution tie-breakers without discarding individually mediocre but complementary origins prematurely.
- Shared coarse-to-fine engine: 4,096 coarse samples, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, local offsets, separate fixed-first and joint branches.
- Tests cover deterministic sampling, double-sided occlusion, marginal second-origin ranking, non-greedy pair ranking, candidate generation, and both search modes.

Blockers:
1. Imported sets can produce zero legal candidates: For every non-floor scene object, the extractor stores the entire object's AABB as an obstacle. Candidate clearance is distance from origin point to those AABBs; candidates within 0.3m are rejected. A point inside an AABB has zero distance. A typical imported model (floor, walls, furniture, props as one SceneObject) has an AABB enclosing the entire room, so every sensible camera origin inside gets zero clearance and is rejected. Affects: complete Maya set imported as one GLB, room shell and furniture combined into one mesh, concave geometry, L-shaped walls, any large model whose AABB contains empty navigable space. Fix: use actual geometry clearance (camera sphere/capsule does not intersect nearby triangles) via coverage BVH point-to-triangle distance, sphere intersection, or shapecast. Obstacle bounds should be per connected mesh or spatial cluster, not per imported set object. Add regression test with one imported object containing room floor, walls, and empty interior.
2. Geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports: Every triangle expanded to a JavaScript object with three independent Vec3 arrays, normal array, IDs, area. For 3 million triangles: positions 3,000,000 × 9 × 4 bytes = 108 MB, normals 3,000,000 × 3 × 4 bytes = 36 MB, minimum packed geometry data 144 MB. Actual representation uses JS objects, arrays, 64-bit numbers, several times larger, then structured-cloned into worker with postMessage creating another enormous representation. BVH recursively sorts and slices JS index arrays. Every triangle intersection allocates several temporary three-element arrays; millions of raycasts create extreme GC pressure. Will probably work on default graybox but expect serious freezing, memory spikes, or crashes on heavy imported projects hitting PanoRef's multi-million-triangle limits. Fix: use compact typed arrays (positions: Float32Array, indices: Uint32Array, normals?: Float32Array, meshRanges: Uint32Array, transforms: Float32Array), transfer ArrayBuffers into worker rather than cloning nested objects. For BVH: use three-mesh-bvh, implement flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning, or build per-mesh BVHs from existing indexed geometries. Avoid expanding indexed vertices into three world-space vertex arrays per triangle.
3. Geometry extraction still blocks the main thread: panel synchronously calls extractCoverageScene(project) before creating/posting to worker. Worker keeps expensive optimizer off UI thread but not scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, structured cloning. On complex model, app may freeze before worker reports first progress event. Fix: move extraction into worker, or make it chunked and yield between meshes.
4. "Apply to selected panorama pair" is conceptually wrong: UI allows optimized origins to be written directly into two existing panorama references. Workspace handler changes their stored origins via updatePanoReference(primaryPanoId, { origin: originA }) and updatePanoReference(secondaryPanoId, { origin: originB }). But existing panorama was rendered/generated from its original origin; changing metadata does not transform image into panorama captured from new position—it merely projects old pixels from wrong point, ruining alignment. Correct workflow for fixed-first: 1) Preserve existing panorama and its origin; 2) Move next capture origin to B; 3) Render new graybox panorama; 4) Inpaint/generate new styled panorama; 5) Import as secondary panorama. For joint mode: 1) Create two-origin capture plan; 2) Move capture origin to A; 3) Capture/render A; 4) Move to B; 5) Capture/render B; 6) Associate each imported result with its actual origin. Do not rewrite origins of already captured panoramas.
5. Reachable upper bound is mathematically inconsistent: reachableCoverage calculated using coarse sample bank and all coarse candidates. Final combined coverage calculated using different fine sample bank generated with seed + 1. Those two percentages placed together in same result and used to calculate reachable efficiency. UI can theoretically show Combined coverage: 83%, Reachable upper bound: 80%, Reachable captured: 100%. Clamp hides impossible ratio but does not repair incompatible estimates. Another fixed-first issue: reachable set calculated before arbitrary first origin is evaluated, so fixed first origin not included in reachable upper bound at all. Fix: use common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, efficiency. For fixed-first, include fixed origin in reachable union. Can still use separate coarse and fine search banks internally, but reported metrics must be evaluated on one shared final bank.
6. Fixed-first does not enforce minimum separation: Joint mode rejects pairs below minimumOriginSeparation. Fixed-first mode does not; rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity, not position or distance. Since first evaluation is separate object, even identical candidate position survives. Add: distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation. Otherwise open set with little marginal difference could return nearly duplicate second origin.

Important refinements:
- "Four-level refinement" is not truly iterative: For every seed, all offsets generated around original seed (seed ± spacing/2, seed ± spacing/4, seed ± spacing/8, seed ± spacing/16). System does not select best half-step result and center quarter-step search around that new result. Still useful multiresolution neighborhood sample, but not coordinate/pattern refinement described in plan. True refinement loop would update center after every level.
- Local candidates can float between floors: Candidate validation only checks whether floor exists somewhere below candidate. Local offsets retain original Y coordinate. On sloped terrain or multilevel sets, offset can move over lower floor while preserving upper floor's camera height, leaving panorama origin floating several meters above new floor. For each offset: 1) find floor under new X/Z; 2) set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters; 3) then perform clearance.
- Optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules: Optimizer evaluates angle and texel density. But when both panoramas visible, actual shader still blends them only by distance. Thus optimizer may prefer source for its frontal angle, while runtime renderer favors closer but more grazing source. Optimized coverage result and visible result do not fully agree. Shader should use same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging.

Testing assessment:
Current tests are good unit tests, but most dangerous cases absent: 1) One large imported object containing entire room; 2) 100k+ triangle performance fixture; 3) reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage invariant; 4) Fixed-first candidate separation; 5) Sloped and multilevel floors; 6) Existing panorama origins remaining immutable; 7) Candidate generation inside concave imported geometry. No GitHub Actions workflow runs attached to latest head, so reported test suite has not been independently enforced in CI.

Bottom line: This push is much better than previously reviewed. Two algorithms truly implemented, joint search not fake or merely greedy. Would preserve most high-level design. Required changes: 1) Replace AABB clearance with actual geometry clearance; 2) Replace object-heavy triangle/BVH data with typed arrays and transferable buffers; 3) Move extraction into worker; 4) Remove ability to relocate existing panorama references; 5) Recalculate reported metrics on one common sample bank; 6) Enforce separation in fixed-first mode; 7) Reproject local refinement candidates onto their floor. After those, optimizer would be strong, credible feature. Right now it should work nicely on ordinary PanoRef primitive sets, but exact scenario motivating this feature—a complex imported production set—is where current implementation is most likely to fail.

Subsequent actions taken:
- Rebasing onto main and resolving PR conflict.
- Adding allowed-floor-region mechanism or at least robust imported-floor component filtering.
- Running one real complex imported-set benchmark and adding full 100K+ optimizer integration test, not merely BVH-construction test.
- Setting goal to accomplish above, then spawning subagent to disprove that goal is fully complete, reporting back what still is lacking, fixing that, and repeating until subagent unable to find holes.
- Removing stale test guarding old distance-only blend heuristic; replacing assertion with one protecting new optimizer-aligned angle/texel-quality selection and dominance modes; targeted regression now passes.
- Unit tests: 42 test files passed, 371 tests passed, duration 41.69s. Lint: tsc --noEmit passed. Build: vite build passed, 1777 modules transformed.
- E2E tests: 22 tests passed (3.5m) using Playwright, covering layout and workflow scenarios including coverage optimizer completing without overflowing Reference drawer.
- Goal smoke test: build → reference → shots → export flow succeeded, producing shot_001_package.zip (33,120,308 bytes).
- Server running on 127.0.0.1:4173 (process ID 33292).

Code changes (git diff --stat):
- 16 files changed, 307 insertions(+), 216 deletions(-)
- Modified: README.md, docs/ui-revamp-regression-audit.md, package.json, src/components/common/ProjectedStylePanel.tsx, src/components/viewers/SceneViewport.tsx, src/domain/defaults.ts, src/domain/types.ts, src/engine/projectedStyleMaterials.ts, src/engine/projectedStyleMath.ts, src/engine/projectionCoverage/surfaceSampler.ts, src/engine/renderers.ts, tests/fixtures/projected-receive-entry.ts, tests/fixtures/projected-style-compile-entry.ts, tests/multiOriginInteraction.test.ts, tests/projectionCoverage.test.ts, tests/projectorOcclusion.test.ts
- New: docs/coverage-optimizer-benchmark.md, scripts/coverage-import-benchmark.mjs

Key implementation details:
- extractCoverageScene now uses compact typed arrays (Float32Array for positions, Uint32Array for indices, Float32Array for mesh matrices) instead of expanding triangles into JS objects.
- Added filterImportedFloorComponents function that groups upward triangles by connected world-space vertices and keeps only components large enough to plausibly support a camera (minimum area 2.5 m², long span 1.5 m, short span 0.65 m). Falls back to largest component if no components meet criteria.
- forEachProjectMesh iterates objects, creates Object3D, traverses for meshes, calls visit for each mesh, then disposes node and yields to main thread.
- copyPositionAttribute copies position data in chunks of 262,144 values, yielding between chunks.
- extractCoverageScene is async, chunked between objects and large buffer ranges so complex imports do not monopolize browser event loop before worker optimization begins.
- Scene data structure: positions (Float32Array), indices (Uint32Array), triangleMeshIds (Uint32Array), meshMatrices (Float32Array), floorTriangleIndices (Uint32Array), floorBounds (Float32Array), bounds, diagonal.
- Floor detection: triangles with area > 1e-8 and normal Y > 0.8 are flagged. Explicit floor objects get flag 2, others get flag 1. If explicit floor seen, use those; otherwise filter imported floor components.
- sampleMeshSurface: deterministic area-weighted Monte Carlo sampling using mulberry32 PRNG, cumulative area array, binary search for triangle selection, barycentric sampling with sqrt(r1) for uniform area distribution.

Test coverage (from tests/projectionCoverage.test.ts):
- Deterministic area-proportional sampling: 5,000 samples on two triangles (1:1 area ratio and 9:1 area ratio), verifies large triangle gets >86% and <92% of samples.
- Double-sided BVH occlusion: raycastAny detects geometry-hidden samples, evaluateOrigin returns individualCoverage 0 for hidden origin.
- Fixed-first marginal union and joint complementary pairs: rankSecondOrigins prefers complementary over redundant, rankAllPairs selects best pair, compareOriginPair unionCoverage = 1.
- Imported-room interior candidates: one imported mesh with floor + 4 walls, candidates generated inside room (distance from center < 0.1), using triangle clearance instead of AABB.
- Extract imported room object retains concave empty interior: prop top (small upward-facing surface) excluded from floor, candidates inside room, all candidates Y < 2.
- One fine validation bank for reachable metrics and fixed-first separation: reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage, reachableEfficiency <= 1, distance between origins >= 1.5.
- Reproject local X/Z offsets onto nearest sloped or multilevel floor: projectCandidateToFloor returns correct Y for upper floor and sloped floor.
- Both search modes: generateOriginCandidates produces >2 candidates all at Y=1.6, fixed-first and joint-pair optimization both work, fixed combinedCoverage > 0.9.

Benchmark documentation (docs/coverage-optimizer-benchmark.md) and script (scripts/coverage-import-benchmark.mjs) added for complex imported-set performance testing.

Current state: Implementation has addressed many original blockers (typed arrays, floor filtering, chunked extraction, triangle clearance, common validation bank, fixed-first separation, floor projection for local offsets). Tests pass (42 files, 371 tests, 41.69s). E2E passes (22 tests, 3.5m). Build succeeds (1777 modules). Smoke test produces valid 33.1 MB package. Server running on 127.0.0.1:4173. However, full 100K+ triangle integration test and real complex imported-set benchmark still needed. Goal is to complete required changes, then have subagent attempt to disprove completeness, fix remaining holes, and repeat until subagent cannot find issues.

Audit round two found one concrete hole: allowed-floor controls remain editable during a running analysis, but edits do not cancel or invalidate the in-flight job, so the old result can appear under newly displayed or invalid bounds. Fix: add a disabled flag to Toggle and disable the restrictFloorRegion toggle plus all floor min/max fields when status === 'running'; update the E2E test to set valid Y bounds, verify the analyze button is enabled, then assert the toggle and bound fields are disabled during the run and re-enabled after. Patch applied, committed as 'Lock coverage floor bounds during analysis' (3 files, 30 insertions, 18 deletions), and pushed to t3code/projector-occlusion (b1834c4..4153429). Verification: lint passes, 51 tests pass (uiFidelity 40, projectionCoverage 11 including the 100k+ triangle fixed-first/joint optimizer test), build 1777 modules / 1,086.44 kB index, and E2E 'coverage optimizer completes' passes on desktop-chromium (1.0m) and phone-390 (34.8s). PR #23 headRefOid 4153429, mergeable MERGEABLE, mergeStateStatus UNSTABLE. Audit round three then reported two stale-state holes unrelated to the in-flight lock: (1) editing bounds after a completed run leaves the old result and origin-apply actions visible even if those origins are outside the newly displayed region; (2) changing the primary panorama does not refresh the untouched default region or invalidate a fixed-first result, so the region remains centered on the previous panorama.
